messages:
acme_ops: We're seeing intermittent 403s calling Redwood's hosted API after we flipped on Azure Private Link + our corporate forward proxy chain. App -> proxy -> PL endpoint -> redwood. Responses sometimes succeed but ~30% fail with 403 and TLS handshake logs show an SNI mismatch. Anyone seen this pattern?

jess_support: Sorry you're hitting this — we'll triage. Can you paste a minimal curl repro and the exact Host/SNI your app is sending? Also which proxy product (F5, Bluecoat, in-house)?

acme_ops: Using Palo Alto proxy chain (transparent), here's a quick repro from a VM in the same subnet as the endpoint:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.1.5.12
```

When it fails, curl shows:
```
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL: certificate subject name (api.some-other-host) does not match target host name 'api.redwood.example.com'
* Server certificate: CN=internal-proxy.local
* HTTP/2 403
```

jess_support: Thanks — that cert CN definitely looks like the proxy re-terminating TLS and presenting its own cert. That would explain the SNI mismatch/cert name. Two quick asks: 1) can you confirm whether the PL endpoint is using NLB (IP target) or Azure's TLS passthrough? 2) grab a tcpdump on the subnet to see the ClientHello SNI going to our endpoint IP.

vikram_network: If the proxy is TLS-terminating then the SNI our backend sees will be the proxy's re-origin SNI (or none) rather than the original Host. On Azure PL you'll often see an NLB/IP target; proxies that re-initiate TLS can rewrite SNI or use default CN. Check your proxy's upstream SNI config — it needs to set SNI to api.redwood.example.com when doing the upstream connection.

acme_ops: Confirmed endpoint is IP-based NLB targets (we used the Private Endpoint network interface). Proxy is in transparent mode but does upstream TLS re-termination to another internal IP. I've asked them to check SNI passthrough.

mike_sre: A couple more things to watch for:
- Private DNS: ensure your privatelink zone resolves api.redwood.example.com to the PL IP consistently across subnets; split-horizon issues can send some clients to public IP and hit proxy chain differently.
- Egress allowlists: if the proxy re-originates to our public egress pool IPs, ensure your firewall allows them; otherwise proxy may return 403 from an internal policy.
- Healthchecks: NLB healthcheck IPs must be allowed into the proxy path or you'll see intermittent failures correlated with health check reapplies.

jess_support: Can you also capture the upstream SNI with this OpenSSL command from a node behind the proxy (if possible)?

```
openssl s_client -connect 10.1.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -msg
```

If the server cert CN is that internal-proxy.local then your proxy is re-terminating TLS. If you can't run it from behind the proxy, run tcpdump on the PL subnet and paste the ClientHello bytes (we can decode).

acme_ops: Ran the openssl command from a host behind the proxy, got the internal-proxy cert. We also tcpdump'd and captured ClientHello — SNI field is empty on the packets arriving at the endpoint. Looks like transparent mode stripped SNI.

vikram_network: That matches. Solutions:
- Configure proxy to preserve/set upstream SNI to api.redwood.example.com, or
- Move to TLS passthrough tunnel for PL endpoint so your proxy doesn't re-terminate, or
- Use mTLS between your proxy and our endpoint (if you want cert-level verification) — requires coordination.

acme_ops: Our security team is reluctant to allow passthrough, wants proxy inspection. They asked if Redwood can accept requests where SNI is missing but host header is correct and auth token valid.

jess_support: We can't change TLS termination expectations on the hosted side — we expect SNI to match the requested hostname for proper routing to the customer's model instance and for cert validation. However, we can work with you: two options — 1) If proxy can set upstream SNI we should be green. 2) If not possible, consider using our Dedicated/Private deployment (VNet/VPC peering) where traffic doesn't traverse inspection proxies, or set up a TLS tunnel (stunnel) from your side.

mike_sre: Also check firewall/proxy allowlist for our public egress ranges (we'll DM you the CIDR block list). Sometimes proxies will inject 403s when an upstream IP isn't allowed.

deploy-bot: deploy completed for internal test harness at 2026-03-16T08:12:01Z — test run queued against 10.1.5.12

acme_ops: Thanks — we'll try configuring upstream-sni and also discuss mTLS option with security. Will update after the proxy team tests. Appreciated :thumbsup:

jess_support: Great — ping us with packet captures or proxy config snippets if you want us to review before trying production.

acme_ops: Follow-up: proxy team set upstream-sni and after a few minutes the 403 rate dropped to 0%. Passing full auth checks now. Thanks everyone! :party_parrot:
